html:
Getúlio Vargas was the leader of Brazil from 1930 to 1945 and again from 1951 to 1954. He built the modern Brazilian state.

A politician from Rio Grande do Sul, he took power in the Revolution of 1930, which ended the rule of the coffee planters of São Paulo and Minas Gerais. In 1937 he set up the Estado Novo, a dictatorship modelled in part on European fascism. He gave workers a minimum wage and labour laws, created state steel and, later, oil companies, Petrobras among them, and sent troops to fight with the Allies in Italy.

Removed by the army in 1945, he was elected president in 1950. Under attack for corruption and facing a new coup, he shot himself in the presidential palace in 1954, leaving a letter saying he left life to enter history. His legacy shaped Brazil until the military regime, and his political heir Juscelino Kubitschek built Brasília.
